title: The Veteran's Hospital Transit
logline: A decommissioned naval hospital ship treating disabled veterans across three systems seeks justice against an industrial consortium whose defective wartime respirators caused systemic poisoning.

roles.description: Commanding officer of the decommissioned hospital ship; proud, weary, and fiercely protective of his disabled patients.
Chief physician aboard the hospital ship; blunt, exhausted, and desperate to prove the chemical cause of veteran poisoning.
Legal director for the regional manufacturing consortium; polished, evasive, and suppressing corporate liability.
A heavily armed private security cruiser stationed to interdict unauthorized medical evidence at gate boundaries.
The administrative gateway controlling transit permits across the three-system cluster.
An abandoned wartime quartermaster depot in a neighboring system containing sealed surplus stock.
The industrial giant that manufactured defective military respirators during the war.
The mutual-aid fraternity of disabled soldiers, nurses, and medical crews.

public_situation: A decommissioned naval hospital ship is refused docking across three star systems as corporate lawyers dispute veteran medical pension claims.
private_truth: The veterans' chronic lung rot was caused by defective cuprite solder used in standard-issue wartime respirators produced by the region's largest manufacturing cartel.

beats.public_change: Customs warnings flash around {role:central_gate_customs_spire} as corporate pickets delay the hospital ship's docking permits.

missions.reason: She pays an outside pilot to collect an impounded crate of veteran respirator masks from a customs warehouse before corporate lawyers can seize and destroy it.
missions.private_fact: Spectrographic tests on the masks showed toxic neuro-heavy metal residues leeching from the intake filter housings.

missions.reason: He hires the pilot to deliver sealed patient triage logs to the port registrar to formally petition against the customs blockade.
missions.private_fact: The triage logs document twelve fatal respiratory arrests occurring within forty-eight hours of docking refusal.

beats.public_change: Consortium pickets shadow veteran support craft throughout the neighboring industrial gateway.

missions.reason: He pays the pilot to destroy a consortium surveillance interceptor and recover encrypted autopsy telemetry intercepted from the hospital's research wards.
missions.private_fact: The ombudsman has bribed regional port coroners to classify veteran deaths as combat hysteria rather than industrial poisoning.

beats.public_change: {role:consortium_ombudsman} files emergency warrants to seal the abandoned naval depot in the second neighboring system.

missions.reason: She hires the pilot to scan surviving crates of unissued wartime respirators in the depot to prove the toxic solder was used across entire regional production runs.
missions.private_fact: The consortium executives knew the solder broke down in humid recycler air but approved shipment to collect massive wartime bonuses.

beats.public_change: {role:consortium_picket_cruiser} blocks the approach to the regional health council tribunal dock, aiming weapons at incoming hospital couriers.

missions.reason: He begs the pilot to disable the picket cruiser's weapons systems before it destroys the courier shuttle carrying the forensic samples to the tribunal.
missions.private_fact: The cruiser captain hails offering a multi-million bearer bond if the pilot vents the respirator samples into the star.

player_choice.prompt: With the picket cruiser disabled and the forensic proof of industrial respirator poisoning assembled across three systems, the pilot must decide whether to deliver the evidence to the tribunal, negotiate a private hospice endowment, or sell out to the consortium.

options.label: Deliver the toxic samples to the regional health tribunal to force the consortium to fund lifelong veteran care
Hand the evidence to the ombudsman in exchange for an irrevocable private endowment funding the hospital ship's wards
Vent the samples and collect the consortium's multi-million payoff

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot delivers the forensic samples to the regional health tribunal.
resolutions.summary: The tribunal finds {role:regional_manufacturing_consortium} guilty of wartime negligence, mandating lifetime medical pensions for thousands of veterans across three systems.

consequences.public_summary: A pilot proved a regional manufacturing cartel poisoned thousands of soldiers with defective wartime respirators.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot brokers a quiet private endowment with the consortium ombudsman.
resolutions.summary: {role:consortium_ombudsman} endows the hospital ship's hospice care in perpetuity. Public scandal is avoided, while {role:hospital_commodore} secures dignified retirement for his crew.

consequences.public_summary: A pilot forced a corporate manufacturing cartel to quietly fund lifetime hospice care for poisoned naval veterans.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot accepts the corporate payoff and vents the samples.
resolutions.summary: Consortium agents erase all forensic records. Poisoned veterans are denied pensions and evicted, while {role:consortium_ombudsman} secures a massive board promotion.

consequences.public_summary: A pilot destroyed forensic evidence proving an industrial cartel sold toxic respirators to wartime troops.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot never intervenes or abandons the defense.
resolutions.summary: Medical life-support filters fail across the convoy. The hospital ship drifts into quarantined transit space, abandoned by regional authorities.

loose_threads.detail: The quartermaster procurement ledger shows a cost-reduction waiver signed by the consortium president six months before the war ended.
The defective respirator solder is traced to a single refinery batch that failed purity tests but was stamped certified anyway.

radio_hooks: Regional customs authorities turn away naval hospital vessel citing expired quarantine permits.
Veterans welfare societies stage protests outside border gate clearance pylons.
Industrial manufacturing consortium posts record quarterly dividends from civilian refits.

voice_direction.hospital_commodore: Low, gravelly, and speaks with rigid naval bearing. Pauses slightly to mask the physical pain of old wounds.
voice_direction.consortium_ombudsman: Polished, breezy, and speaks with practiced diplomatic charm that turns icy and dismissive when defied.
voice_direction.fleet_medical_surgeon: Harried, blunt, and cuts off administrative pleasantries to demand concrete medicine and fuel counts.
